terms.gloss: cast one’s eyes on, glance at
evidence: Cic. Clu. 54; Lael. 9 (Lewis & Short, s.v. conjiciō)
terms.comment: To turn one’s eyes on someone or something, often for a moment.

evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.162 (Lewis & Short, s.v. strictim)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: Ciceronian, but very rare; strictim is “grazingly, in passing”.
At a glance is ūnō aspectū; at first glance, prīmō aspectū.

phrases.latin: intellegēns dīcendī exīstimātor ūnō aspectū et praeteriēns dē ōrātōre saepe jūdicat
phrases.english: an expert judge of speaking often makes up his mind about a speaker at a single glance, in passing

phrases.latin: ē quibus prīmō aspectū voluptātem cēpī, quod erant ā tē ipsō scrīptae
phrases.english: at first glance your letters gave me pleasure, because they were written in your own hand

sources: Lewis & Short: conicio · Lewis & Short: strictim · Lewis & Short: aspectus
